# `ossready doctor` checks

`ossready doctor` runs 30 checks, 8 required and 22 recommended. 19 of them always run. The other 11 run only when they apply: 8 `package.json` checks for npm publish readiness, `workflow-actions`, `readme-badges` and `managed-files`.

Required checks make `ossready doctor` exit with code 1 when they fail. Recommended checks are warnings that fail the run only with `--strict`. The Fix column says whether `ossready doctor --fix` can fix a failing check: yes, partial (only in some cases, see the check) or no (report only).

Print this catalogue in a terminal with `ossready doctor --list`, or as JSON with `ossready doctor --list --json`. Every command and option is in [commands.md](commands.md).

| Check                | Title                                      | Level       | Fix     |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------- |
| `readme`             | README                                     | required    | yes     |
| `license`            | License                                    | required    | partial |
| `code-of-conduct`    | Code of Conduct                            | required    | yes     |
| `contributing`       | Contributing guide                         | required    | yes     |
| `security`           | Security policy                            | required    | yes     |
| `issue-templates`    | Issue templates                            | required    | yes     |
| `pr-template`        | Pull request template                      | required    | yes     |
| `ci`                 | CI workflow                                | required    | yes     |
| `support`            | Support resources                          | recommended | yes     |
| `changelog`          | Changelog                                  | recommended | yes     |

| `pkg-name-version`   | package.json name and version              | recommended | no      |
| `pkg-description`    | package.json description                   | recommended | no      |
| `pkg-license`        | package.json license                       | recommended | no      |
| `pkg-links`          | package.json repository, bugs and homepage | recommended | partial |

| `pkg-files`          | Published files allowlist                  | recommended | no      |
| `pkg-entry`          | Entry points (main / exports / bin)        | recommended | no      |

## Details

### `readme`

README (required). A README that explains what the project does and how to use it.

- Looks at: `README.md`, `README`, `README.markdown`, `README.rst` or `README.txt` in the repo root, `.github/` or `docs/` (any case)
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `README.md` from the template, with the badge block.

### `license`

License (required). A license file, so others can legally reuse the code.

- Looks at: `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md`, `LICENSE.txt`, `LICENCE`, `LICENCE.md` or `COPYING` in the repo root (any case)
- Runs: always
- Fix: partial. Writes `LICENSE` only when the license is known (`MIT` or `Apache-2.0` in `package.json`, or `--license`): picking one is your call.

### `code-of-conduct`

Code of Conduct (required). A Code of Conduct that sets community standards.

- Looks at: `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT` or `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.txt` in the repo root, `.github/` or `docs/` (any case)
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` (Contributor Covenant 2.1).

### `contributing`

Contributing guide (required). A guide that tells contributors how to set up, test and submit changes.

- Looks at: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CONTRIBUTING`, `CONTRIBUTING.txt` or `CONTRIBUTING.rst` in the repo root, `.github/` or `docs/` (any case)
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### `security`

Security policy (required). A security policy that explains how to report vulnerabilities privately.

- Looks at: `SECURITY.md`, `SECURITY` or `SECURITY.txt` in the repo root, `.github/` or `docs/` (any case)
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `SECURITY.md` (with `--security-email` when given).

### `issue-templates`

Issue templates (required). Issue templates or Issue Forms that keep bug reports and feature requests actionable.

- Looks at: a `.yml`, `.yaml` or `.md` file in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` other than `config.yml`, or `ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md` in the repo root, `.github/` or `docs/`
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes the bug report and feature request Issue Forms plus `config.yml`.

### `pr-template`

Pull request template (required). A pull request template that asks for context, tests and a checklist.

- Looks at: `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` or `pull_request_template.md` in the repo root, `.github/` or `docs/`, or a `.md` file in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`.

### `ci`

CI workflow (required). A GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every push or pull request.

- Looks at: the contents of `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `*.yaml`: a `push` or `pull_request` trigger
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; review it before pushing, since it runs the lint, format:check, test and build scripts.

### `support`

Support resources (recommended). Support resources that point users to the right place for questions and help.

- Looks at: `SUPPORT.md`, `SUPPORT` or `SUPPORT.txt` in the repo root, `.github/` or `docs/` (any case)
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `SUPPORT.md`.

### `changelog`

Changelog (recommended). A changelog that records notable changes per release (Keep a Changelog).

- Looks at: `CHANGELOG.md`, `CHANGELOG`, `HISTORY.md` or `CHANGES.md` in the repo root or `docs/` (any case)
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `CHANGELOG.md`.

### `codeowners`

CODEOWNERS (recommended). A CODEOWNERS file, so maintainers are asked for reviews automatically.

- Looks at: `CODEOWNERS` in the repo root, `.github/` or `docs/`
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.github/CODEOWNERS` (with the GitHub owner when known).

### `dependabot`

Dependabot config (recommended). Dependabot config that keeps dependencies and GitHub Actions up to date.

- Looks at: `.github/dependabot.yml` or `.github/dependabot.yaml`
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.github/dependabot.yml` (npm and GitHub Actions, weekly).

### `codeql`

CodeQL code scanning (recommended). CodeQL code scanning that catches security bugs.

- Looks at: the contents of `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `*.yaml`: a `github/codeql-action/init` or `analyze` step (an `upload-sarif` step alone does not count)
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`.

### `scorecard`

OpenSSF Scorecard (recommended). An OpenSSF Scorecard workflow that tracks supply-chain security.

- Looks at: the contents of `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `*.yaml`: `ossf/scorecard-action`
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml`.

### `funding`

Funding links (recommended). Funding links that show a Sponsor button on the repo.

- Looks at: `.github/FUNDING.yml` or `.github/FUNDING.yaml`
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.github/FUNDING.yml` (with the GitHub owner when known).

### `citation`

Citation metadata (recommended). Citation File Format metadata for GitHub's Cite this repository button.

- Looks at: `CITATION.cff` in the repo root
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `CITATION.cff`.

### `editorconfig`

EditorConfig (recommended). An EditorConfig file for consistent indentation and line endings across editors.

- Looks at: `.editorconfig` in the repo root
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.editorconfig`.

### `gitignore`

.gitignore (recommended). A `.gitignore` that keeps build output and secrets out of git.

- Looks at: `.gitignore` in the repo root
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `.gitignore`.

### `agents-md`

AI agent instructions (recommended). An `AGENTS.md` that gives AI coding agents the setup, test and style rules.

- Looks at: `AGENTS.md` in the repo root
- Runs: always
- Fix: yes. Writes `AGENTS.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` with the detected package manager's commands.

### `pkg-name-version`

package.json name and version (recommended). `package.json` has a `name` and a semver `version`; npm cannot publish without them.

- Looks at: `package.json` `name` and `version`
- Runs: only when a `package.json` exists, is valid JSON and is not `"private": true`
- Fix: no. Report only: edit `package.json` by hand.

### `pkg-description`

package.json description (recommended). `package.json` has a one-line `description` for npm search and the package page.

- Looks at: `package.json` `description`
- Runs: only when a `package.json` exists, is valid JSON and is not `"private": true`
- Fix: no. Report only: edit `package.json` by hand.

### `pkg-license`

package.json license (recommended). `package.json` `license` is an SPDX id that matches the LICENSE file when that file is recognisably MIT or Apache-2.0.

- Looks at: `package.json` `license` and the `LICENSE` file in the repo root
- Runs: only when a `package.json` exists, is valid JSON and is not `"private": true`
- Fix: no. Report only: edit `package.json` by hand.

### `pkg-links`

package.json repository, bugs and homepage (recommended). `package.json` has `repository`, `bugs` and `homepage`, so npm links back to the repo.

- Looks at: `package.json` `repository`, `bugs` and `homepage`
- Runs: only when a `package.json` exists, is valid JSON and is not `"private": true`
- Fix: partial. Adds the missing links when the GitHub owner is known (`--github-owner`, GitHub URLs in `package.json`, or the `origin` remote); existing values are never changed.

### `pkg-engines`

package.json engines.node (recommended). `package.json` declares the supported Node.js range in `engines.node`.

- Looks at: `package.json` `engines.node`
- Runs: only when a `package.json` exists, is valid JSON and is not `"private": true`
- Fix: no. Report only: edit `package.json` by hand.

### `pkg-files`

Published files allowlist (recommended). A `files` allowlist or an `.npmignore`, so npm publish does not ship everything.

- Looks at: `package.json` `files`, then `.npmignore` in the repo root
- Runs: only when a `package.json` exists, is valid JSON and is not `"private": true`
- Fix: no. Report only: edit `package.json` by hand.

### `pkg-entry`

Entry points (main / exports / bin) (recommended). `main`, `exports` or `bin` point at relative paths inside the package, not at `.ts` sources, and are covered by `files`.

- Looks at: `package.json` `main`, `exports`, `bin` and `files`
- Runs: only when a `package.json` exists, is valid JSON and is not `"private": true`
- Fix: no. Report only: edit `package.json` by hand.

### `pkg-publish-access`

publishConfig.access for scoped packages (recommended). Scoped packages set `publishConfig.access`, since npm publishes them as restricted by default.

- Looks at: `package.json` `name` and `publishConfig.access`
- Runs: only when a `package.json` exists, is valid JSON and is not `"private": true`
- Fix: no. Report only: edit `package.json` by hand.

### `workflow-actions`

Current GitHub Action versions (recommended). Known actions are not pinned to an older major than ossready's templates use; commit-SHA pins are info only.

- Looks at: `uses:` lines in `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `*.yaml`, compared with `src/templates/actions.ts`
- Runs: only when `.github/workflows/*.yml` or `*.yaml` files exist
- Fix: no. Report only: bump the pins or let Dependabot do it; `ossready sync --write` updates ossready-managed workflows.

### `readme-badges`

README badges (recommended). The badge block in `README.md` matches what `ossready badges` would generate.

- Looks at: the `ossready:badges` start and end markers in the root `README.md`
- Runs: only when a root `README.md` exists
- Fix: partial. Runs `ossready badges --write` when the GitHub owner is known; a README with only one marker is left for you to fix.

### `managed-files`

ossready-managed files up to date (recommended). Files that start with the ossready marker line match the current templates.

- Looks at: the files `ossready sync` manages (workflows, `dependabot.yml`, Issue Forms, the PR template and `.editorconfig`)
- Runs: only when at least one file carries the ossready marker line
- Fix: yes. Runs `ossready sync --write` for stale marked files (never `--force` or `--add-missing`).
